criteria.name: Register match
criteria.reason: All-caps button label matches LEM-011 pattern exactly. The register is appropriate for low-stakes interface action.

criteria.name: Humour boundary
criteria.reason: No humour present. Low-stakes action copy correctly avoids jokes, consistent with approved low-stakes examples.

criteria.name: Plain language calibration
criteria.reason: Uses concrete verb 'get' and avoids insurance jargon. Follows the vocabulary preference for direct language without needing translation.

criteria.name: Direct address
criteria.reason: The draft 'GET YOUR QUOTE' has no named subject (pet, person, car, home) available from an interface state to address directly, unlike LEM-009 which had an email or LEM-020/022 which addressed a specific reader situation. There's no neighbouring context provided showing a named addressee was available but omitted.

criteria.name: Character budget
criteria.reason: No declared interface character limit is provided for this string, so fit cannot be assessed against a hard limit.

criteria.name: Action verb consistency
criteria.reason: 'GET YOUR QUOTE' uses a concrete action verb consistent with approved examples like 'GET DISCOUNTS' and 'FINALIZE PAYMENT', matching the pattern of short, all-caps, verb-led button labels used in the product flow.

compliance.reason: The draft consists solely of the button label 'GET YOUR QUOTE', which is an isolated navigation/call-to-action element with an appropriate action verb naming what happens (getting a quote). It contains no promises of outcomes, no claims about how Lemonade judges customers, no data/price/coverage/eligibility assertions, and no attributed quotes or factual claims requiring a source. Per instructions, an isolated navigation or button label is not to be failed for lacking surrounding copy, a source, or a disclaimer. None of the compliance prohibitions (guarantee, disclaimer removal, unsupported judgement claim, contradiction, unsourced attributed claim) are triggered by this text.
